Introduction
PRISM is the parent company behind a portfolio of hospitality, travel, and technology brands, including OYO, Belvilla by OYO, DanCenter, Motel 6, Sunday, Palette, Townhouse, Clubhouse, Checkmyguest, Made Comfy, Innov8, Traum by OYO, and Admiral Strand.
We recognize the important role security researchers play in helping protect our platforms, products, customers, partners, and users.
Through this Vulnerability Disclosure Program, we welcome responsible security research and encourage the reporting of security vulnerabilities that may impact assets owned and operated by PRISM and its affiliated brands.
We appreciate the efforts of the security community in helping us identify and remediate security issues responsibly.
Please note that this is a Vulnerability Disclosure Program (VDP) and does not offer monetary rewards or bug bounties.

Program Details
We appreciate the efforts of independent security researchers who help us improve the security of our systems.
If you believe you have discovered a security vulnerability in an in-scope asset, please submit a report with sufficient detail for our team to reproduce and validate the issue.
We are committed to reviewing all legitimate submissions and working with researchers to understand, triage, and remediate confirmed vulnerabilities.
Good luck, and happy hunting!
Severity Assessment
PRISM follows HackerOne's severity rating methodology when evaluating reported vulnerabilities.
Please note that severity may be adjusted based on factors such as:
Exploitability
Business impact
Data sensitivity
Required privileges
Environmental controls
Real-world risk
The final severity determination rests with the PRISM Security Team.
Testing Guidelines
If account registration is required, please use your @wearehackerone.com email alias whenever possible.
Only test against assets explicitly listed as in scope.
If you identify a vulnerability that provides access to sensitive data, internal systems, or privileged functionality, do not proceed beyond what is necessary to demonstrate impact.
Avoid actions that may negatively affect the availability, integrity, or performance of our systems.
If using automated scanning tools, include your HackerOne username in requests whenever feasible using a custom header: X-HackerOne: your_username
Reporting Guidelines
To help us investigate efficiently, please ensure your report contains:
Clear description of the issue
Affected asset(s)
Reproduction steps
Proof of Concept (PoC)
Relevant screenshots, logs, or evidence
Impact assessment
Additional guidelines:
Submit one vulnerability per report unless multiple issues must be chained together to demonstrate impact.
Multiple vulnerabilities resulting from a single underlying root cause may be treated as one issue.
Duplicate reports will generally be closed in favor of the first reproducible submission.
Researchers may be requested to assist with validation or remediation verification activities.
Rules of Engagement
By participating in this program, you agree to:
Keep all findings and communications confidential.
Not disclose vulnerabilities to any third party without prior written authorization.
Not access, modify, destroy, or exfiltrate data that does not belong to you.

Introduction
ASSA ABLOY Opening Solutions Americas and/or any of its group companies (together or individually, "ASSA ABLOY Americas") believes that the disclosure of vulnerabilities is essential to improving the quality of our products and services. ASSA ABLOY Americas values the insights of the security research community and welcomes disclosure and collaboration.
Through our responsible disclosure process, ASSA ABLOY Americas will work with security researchers and other vulnerability investigators to make our products and services more secure by providing a mechanism to privately report vulnerabilities with legitimacy and integrity. Responsible disclosure ensures that security infrastructure is tested and proven reliable. This process allows us to work collaboratively with researchers to identify and mitigate vulnerabilities quickly in an ever-changing security environment.
We appreciate your contributions to protecting our customers, users, and businesses.

Ratings / Rewards
For the initial prioritization and rating of findings, this program will use the HackerOne Vulnerability Rating Taxonomy. It's important to note that in some cases a vulnerability priority will be modified based on its likelihood or impact. In any instance where an issue is downgraded, a full, detailed explanation will be provided to the researcher — along with the opportunity to appeal and make a case for a higher priority.
Credentials
Please sign up for your own accounts using your @wearehackerone.com email address.
Out of Scope
Please note that we cannot authorize out-of-scope testing on third-party products or services. Vulnerabilities discovered in third-party products or services should be reported to the appropriate vendor.
The following are explicitly out of scope:
HTML Injection
Rate limiting
HTTP headers without an associated, exploitable vulnerability
Reporting
Please use the Report Vulnerability tab to submit a finding, or visit our partner HackerOne at https://hackerone.com/vulnerability-rating-taxonomy.
Disclosure
ASSA ABLOY Americas will follow standard industry practices for coordinated and responsible vulnerability disclosure. We ask all vulnerability reporters to do the same — please allow ASSA ABLOY Americas the opportunity to verify and remediate reported vulnerabilities and to notify affected customers and users before you disclose or share the vulnerability or exploitation methods with any third party.
ASSA ABLOY Americas product security advisories will be made publicly available at https://www.assaabloydss.com/en/resource-center/security-center/product-security-advisories and/or communicated directly to affected customers.
Safe Harbor
ASSA ABLOY believes that ethical security research performed in good faith provides an invaluable public service and has therefore provided this safe harbor program to encourage lawful, authorized security testing of our products and services.
Accordingly, ASSA ABLOY will not initiate, pursue, or recommend any law enforcement or civil lawsuits related to the specific actions taken by you to discover a security vulnerability, provided that such actions were undertaken in good faith, for the sole purpose of improving the overall security of our products and services, and not for any nefarious or otherwise unlawful purpose.
